messages.subject: is R package (and lavaan more specifically) ready to be used for serious, real-world research?
parts:
I received the comments from a reviewer who says that I must redo all the analysis for a contracted work using Mplus or SAS because the R package in general and especially lavaan is not ready to be used for serious governmental contracts. Obviously, he is seriously biased. However, this is what he says and the client is worried! This is a big problem for me, because I will need to redo 20 days of work.... and I will need to buy Mplus or SAS! How can I respond to him? How can I reassure the client? Are lavaan results reliable? How do we know that?
Please help with ideas!!!!

messages.subject: Re: is R package (and lavaan more specifically) ready to be used for serious, real-world research?
parts:
On 11/03/2014 12:47 PM, Jason Lamprianou wrote:
> Are lavaan results reliable? How do we know that?

Some reflections:

- the advantage of open-source software packages is that everyone can
inspect the source code; there is nothing hidden. How can we know for
sure that commercial software is reliable?

- all software packages contain bugs; this includes commercial software.
The advantage of open-source software packages is that everyone can
inspect the source code; there is nothing hidden. Commercial packages
correct bugs/issues with every update, but they will usually not mention
what they have changed/fixed. On the other hand, most open-source
packages (including lavaan) are very explicit about possible
bugs/issues that may have been present in a certain version.

Yves.

messages.author: 061281a8cdc1f42e
messages.subject: Re: is R package (and lavaan more specifically) ready to be used for serious, real-world research?
parts:
Hi Jason,
This may not help with the reviewer in question, but I've found lavaan's 'mimic' functions to be quite helpful in convincing others of the package's reliability. You can run your analysis with lavaan and then use the 'mimic=mplus' option to run the model as Mplus would. I can't seem to find this slide deck anywhere, but Yves has a great presentation where the Mplus and EQS algorithms are covered in detail and how they are implemented in lavaan. You could even go so far as to pull up the lavaan code and show the reviewer that what lavaan does is identical to what the Mplus manual states (as Yves said, one of the great benefits of open source).
